title: PHP fatal-error backtraces can retain or access freed memory
summary: Magic-method backtrace argument collection can access freed values and permit code execution. A separate shutdown path can repopulate a backtrace global after cleanup, causing later requests to use stale memory.

severity.rationale: The magic-method path has confirmed code execution under specific runtime settings and address assumptions. The shutdown-global path demonstrates crashes, without code execution through those entry points.

exposure: Magic methods require fatal_error_backtraces=1 and zend.exception_ignore_args=0; php.ini-production blocks that demonstrated path. The shutdown issue needs specific INI restoration diagnostics and an early diagnostic in a later request on the same worker.

params.instructions: Check PHP engine version and the documented exposure conditions against the cited advisory.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade to 8.5.13. Temporarily disable fatal_error_backtraces administratively and restart workers; prevent request-specific overrides from re-enabling it.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
